findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition overwrites the previous method
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier four-argument `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers using the old width/height signature will either raise ArgumentError if they pass an options hash as a fifth argument, or have the height argument treated as the options hash, causing a TypeError when `optimize` calls `opts[:allow_animation]`. This breaks the public API and any existing callers.

findings.title: In-place downsizing uses the same path as an open tempfile
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` rewrites the uploaded file in place while the `tempfile` object remains open. Subsequent code uses `tempfile.size` and passes `tempfile` to `Upload.create_for` without reopening or rewinding it. If ImageMagick/gifsicle/ImageOptim replace the file, truncate it, or leave the descriptor at an old offset, the loop may read stale size/content and the upload may store the original or corrupted file. Use a separate output file and then reopen/rewind/replace the tempfile.

findings.title: Downsizing loop ignores failures and final size
findings.body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize` up to five times but ignores its boolean result and proceeds to create the upload even if every attempt fails or the file is still larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`. This can accept oversized/unchanged images or fail later with an unrelated error. It should check the return value and final size and return an error when the image cannot be reduced enough.

findings.title: Remote URL downloads are hardcoded to 10 MB and bypass site limits
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` now downloads remote uploads up to 10 MB regardless of `max_image_size_kb` or attachment-size settings. The later automatic downsizing only applies to files recognized as images, so non-image URL uploads can be fetched and possibly processed above configured limits, and even image downloads can consume more bandwidth/memory than the site allows. The download limit should be derived from the appropriate site setting/type.

findings.title: Client-side upload size validation is hardcoded to 10 MB
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` now uses `10 * 1024` instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. The client no longer enforces or displays the configured limits for images/attachments; users may be allowed to upload files the server will reject, or prevented from uploading files the server would allow. The same hardcoding in the 413 handler makes error messages inaccurate.
